description.value:
Compatibility: Bestial

When folks describe minotaurs, they often think first of their bull-like features, their formidable, almost top-heavy stature, and their horn. Valley-Hoof minotaurs are often what people envision. Found most often amid rolling hills and fertile valleys, valley-hooves are the most bovine of their kind, with large-nosed snouts on large heads, long horns, bent backs, and skin-tight pelts. Their stout build makes tough work like mining, hauling, and smithing look easy, and the abundance these boons bring make for a hale constitution. Their hooves are the toughest to crack and are uniquely flat, garnering them the misnomer “flat-hoof” minotaurs. This lets them distribute their weight across a larger area and across more lifting muscles, giving them more of a grip, even on mud.

Adding to the bovine comparisons, valley-hooves are generally thought of as docile minotaurs. Devious types sometimes mistake valley-hooves for pushovers and easy targets—a misconception short-lived after realizing a valley-hoof minotaur’s reaction to provocation is as fearsome as any other.

If your core race does not already grant you Horns, you can choose to replace either the “Mighty Physique” racial trait with the @Compendium[undertaking.abilities.HF5TGW1UQJY6J1GK]{Lesser Horns} alternate heritage trait from the start of this section.
